So He who is able to make differences among them, though they come from one water, is not thereby far-fetched in that He should make the proofs in the Book and other than it a light for one person and blindness for another.

[p. 45] Having mentioned the diversity of what comes from water, and having put it first because it is the origin of colouring just as it is the origin of creation, He followed it with the colouring from the earth, which is also one single thing. He said, mentioning what is the hardest of the earth and furthest from receptivity to being affected, and separating it from the former because water has no effect on it: ﴿And among﴾, that is, and of what We have created of ﴿the mountains are streaks﴾, that is, paths, marks and intersecting lines; ﴿white and red﴾. Perhaps He expressed them by this rather than "paths" (*turuq*) to indicate that among their strangeness is that they do not wear away and their colours do not fade over the length of time, as is customary with most things whose age grows old. *Al-jadd* (with a fatha), *al-jiddah* (with a kasra), and *al-jadad* (with a vowel on the middle letter): the surface of the earth; its plural is *jidad* (with a kasra). *Al-juddah* (with a damma): the path, the mark, and the line on the back of a donkey which differs from its colour; its plural is *judad*, like *ghuddah* and *ghudad*, *uddah* and *udad*, *muddah* and *mudad*. *Al-jadad* (with the vowel on the middle letter): what rises from the sand, the likeness of a growth on a camel's neck, and firm level ground. *Al-jadjad* (with a fatha): level ground.

Since what is more eloquent than this is that those streaks, in themselves, are not uniform in the places of that colour with which they are coloured, He (exalted) said, indicating that each of these two colours has not reached the extreme of purity: ﴿of varying shades﴾; and they are [p. 46] from the earth, and it is one; and since He had put first what was strange in the colours of the earth, because it was other than its original colour, He followed it with what is closer to the dust, which is the origin of its colour.

Since the root *gh-r-b* revolves around concealment, which entails obscurity, taken from the setting (*ghurub*) of the sun, and blackness follows from it, for this reason the black is emphasised with *ghirbib* as an intensification of *gharab* (on the pattern of *farah*), that is, black, for the intensification of its blackness. And since the intended meaning is description with the utmost blackness, differing from other things, He (exalted) said, conjoining it to "white": ﴿and intensely black﴾, that is, of the streaks also; ﴿black﴾. So He put the emphasis first, because the context indicates that the original expression is "and black, intensely black". So He omitted the first, so that it would precede the word it emphasises, since it is a follower; and He indicated it by the second, so that the emphasis would be intensified to the utmost degree, by stating it explicitly after its implicit mention (*al-idmar*, the implicit mention, and *al-izhar*, the explicit mention). This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "The most intense blackness is the *gharibib*," narrated from him by al-Bukhari, because pure blackness in the earth is rare, and among it is that which clothes are dyed with, with nothing else alongside it, so that it becomes in the utmost blackness. This occurs in the city of Fuwwah, Masir and others, of the lands of Egypt near to them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 35, verse 28:

When he (may God be exalted) had confirmed this by what indicates its sincerity, he put first the mention of difference (ikhtilaf) concerning it. When he mentioned what is mostly water, of what changes into something else far removed from water, and followed it with pure earth, he concluded with what is mostly earth, of what changes into something that is at the furthest extreme from earth. So he said: ﴿And of mankind﴾, meaning those who move by action and choice, ﴿and the beasts﴾. Since the dabba (beast) was originally whatever crawls on the earth, and then its use became predominant for what is ridden, he said ﴿and the cattle﴾ so that it would clearly encompass everything, ﴿their colours differ﴾, meaning the colours of that part which the word "min" (of) has conveyed. ﴿Likewise﴾, meaning like the fruits and the lands: some of them are of one colour and some of them are of many colours, although everything mentioned here is, from the lands, uniform in its substances yet different in its attributes, and its relation to them and to the sky is one. So where is the rule of natures?

When it was established by this proof that He, glorified is He, acts by choice, so that He does what He wills, and to whom He wills, what He wills, He makes one thing light for one people and blindness for another. This was an incitement to serve Him and a warning of His might, glorified and exalted is He, and hallowed is He, for every person of understanding. The context was the warning of the one who fears in the unseen, so it is established that the warning by this Qur'an is for a people whose fear God has willed to be genuine fear, and for a people whose hardness God has willed to be hardness. The soul turned to seeking a law by which one knows who fears and who does not fear. So He said, by way of inference from that, to repel the thought of one who supposes that an ignorant person could be a friend (of God): ﴿Only those fear God﴾, meaning the One who possesses all perfection, and there is no perfection for anyone except from Him. It indicates that everyone other than Him is in His grip and under His subjugation, by His saying: ﴿from among His servants﴾. Then He mentioned the locus of the benefit, which is the one whose warning benefits, and He said: ﴿the scholars﴾, meaning not others, even if they are worshippers, and even if their worship reaches whatever it may reach, because no one truly fears another except with knowledge of Him, and the ignorant do not know Him. So the meaning becomes as if it were said: "The warning benefits only the people of fear, and only the scholars fear." The scholar is the jurist who acts upon his knowledge. Al-Suhrawardi said in the third chapter of his ʿAwarif: "Knowledge is thus negated from one who does not fear God, as when one says: 'Only a Baghdadi enters the house,' so the entry of a non-Baghdadi into the house is negated." This is the meaning of the well-known reading.

Since the cause of fear is veneration and reverence, and since everyone reveres only the one who has revered him, and since it has been established that the scholars revere God, and the cause of their reverence for Him is His reverence for them, this was the meaning of the other reading. It was as if it were said: "The warning benefits only the one who reveres God, and God reveres him because of his knowledge." Our shaykh, the verifier of his age, the qadi of the Shafi'is in Egypt, Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Qayati, was asked about the explanation of this reading, and he lowered his head briefly, then raised his head and said:

*I revere you out of reverence, though I have no power over you,*
*but the fullness of an eye is its beloved.*

When it was established by this context that He, glorified is He, is the doer of these contrary things, he gave the reason for that, to convey that His power over everything He wills is like His power over Him (Himself), by His saying, by way of emphasis, as an alert that nothing is difficult for Him, glorified is He, and that He is worthy to be feared; for this reason he manifested the Greatest Name: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning the One encompassing majesty and honour, ﴿is Mighty﴾, meaning victorious over all His affairs. Since this inspires dread of His might and necessitates fear of Him, as it conveys that He withholds His mercy from those who do not fear, He encouraged them by His saying: ﴿Forgiving﴾, in that He erases the sins of whomever He wills among them, so that he turns his heart toward Him; and this too is among the meanings of "might."

Having established this, the listener's curiosity is aroused to know who the scholars are. It is as if it was said: "They are those who preserve the Book of God, in knowledge and in action." So it was said, "What is their reward?" And He said, emphasizing it as a rebuttal to those among the disbelievers and other disobedient people who think they are among the losers because of what they lost of their worldly life:

﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of God﴾: that is, they renew the recitation at all times, persistently and steadfastly, whenever some part of the Qur'an is revealed and after its complete revelation, so that this becomes their custom and their way, whether with understanding or without understanding. ﴿The Book of God﴾: that is, the one to which no intelligent person should turn in preference to any other, because of its attributes of beauty and majesty. When He mentioned the cause, which has no equivalent cause, (p-50) He mentioned the best thing to which it is linked. So He said, indicating continuity by the expression "establishing" and the realization of the act by the past tense:

﴿and they establish the prayer﴾: that is, and it (the prayer) forbids indecency and wrongdoing; so they converse with God in it through His speech. When He mentioned the connection between them and the Creator, He mentioned their kindness to creation. So He said, indicating the occurrence of the act by the past tense, and its constancy by "in secret and in public," turning the speech toward the manifestation of greatness, as a reminder that provision comes from Him alone, not by the power of anyone other than Him, nor by anything else:

﴿and spend from what We have provided for them﴾: that is, by Our power and Our strength, not by anything of their own doing, in all that pleases Us. It indicates their persistence in spending, even if it leads to the depletion of wealth, by His saying: ﴿in secret and in public﴾. He expressed the first with the present tense, because its revelation was before completion; and to declare the repetition of recitation as an act of worship and study, because the Qur'an, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "...is more prone to escape than camels in their tethers." Muslim narrated it from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him). In the second and third, he used the past tense, urging haste in doing the act. From this it is established that He made for the act of the heart, which is fear (khashyah), one proof by the tongue, another by the limbs, and a third by wealth.

When He settled them in the highest station, making known that they are the people of knowledge who fear God, and since a servant has no claim upon his master for anything, He said, alerting to the blessing of the second enduring (reward), which is the mother of all blessings and the great outcome intended in itself:

﴿They hope﴾: that is, (p-51) in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿for a commerce﴾: that is, for what they have done, ﴿that will never perish﴾: that is, will never become unsaleable or be lost; rather it remains, because it has been deposited with One before whom deposits are never lost, and it is profitable and gainful, because He is perfectly powerful, all-encompassing in knowledge, and possesses absolute self-sufficiency.

When the purpose of their not being destroyed was their preservation and their survival until the Day of their meeting with Him, he gave the reason by saying, limiting himself to the pronoun (because the context concerns the believers, and for this reason he turned it to the third-person pronoun, since their faith is in the unseen): ﴿That He may pay them﴾, meaning: for their being pure of hypocrisy before Him, may He be exalted, in this world, if He wills, or in the Hereafter, or in both; ﴿their rewards﴾, meaning: for those deeds; ﴿and increase them﴾, meaning: beyond what He made, by His grace and blessing, a right for them upon Himself; ﴿of His bounty﴾, meaning: an increase for which they have no causal contribution at all, but rather it comes after He has bestowed upon them what corresponds to their deeds, which they know to be their recompense, multiplied tenfold for each one and beyond. Since their deeds are never free of some admixture, even if they are sincere, their reward is not something they deserve because of their own deeds, since it comes from His grace, may He be exalted. He gave the reason for paying them in full by saying, emphasizing (to inform that nothing can encompass people except His pardon, because no one will ever measure God by His true measure, however hard he strives, and even if He were to hold the most devout of His servants accountable for the shortcomings that occur from him, He would destroy him): ﴿Indeed, He is Forgiving﴾, meaning: by erasing the deficiency from the deed; ﴿Appreciative﴾, meaning: (p-52) He accepts it and increases upon it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 35, verse 31:

Since the verse's meaning is that the scholars are the bearers of the Book, and He—glory be to Him—began with the lowest of their ranks, and this was among the things that encourage one toward the Book, He followed it with an encouragement that is higher than it. So He said, linking it to His previous statement, in establishing the second principle, which is the Messengership: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾ [Fatir: 24], and He emphasized it to repel the denial of those who deny it: ﴿And that which We have revealed﴾; i.e., with what We possess of greatness; ﴿to you﴾; and He made its rank clear by the manifestation of greatness. And He said, explaining the revelation: ﴿of the Book﴾; i.e., the one that combines the good of both abodes. Since the Book is not subject to any kind of change, because it is an attribute of One who does not change, He said: ﴿it is the truth﴾; i.e., perfect in steadfastness and in the correspondence of reality to it, not other than it of speech. And He emphasized its truthfulness by His saying: ﴿confirming what is before it﴾; i.e., of the earlier books, which the Messengers who call to Allah came with, supported by clear proofs and decisive evidences.

Since He—glory be to Him—indicated that knowledge is the established reality, and that whatever else is effacement and falsehood, and indicated that those who recite His Book, which is knowledge, are the scholars, and that others, even if they exist, are more like the non-existent, and indicated that the earlier books, even though they are true, are not in the perfection of the Qur'an, because the matter, as long as it has not been sealed, an addition to it is expected; unlike when the sealing has occurred, for then no addition is awaited after it; and it may have appeared to someone, regarding some of those characterized by this, otherwise—He (Exalted is He) said, informing that the consideration is with what is with Him, not with what appears to the servants; and He emphasized it, alerting that this meaning is among those on which the fingers are tied, even if most people perceive otherwise, He manifested the Greatest Name, because of the need of those who are informed here for it, since they are both the righteous and the wicked: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾; i.e., He to whom belong all attributes of perfection. And since a person is most knowledgeable about the one who raises him, especially if he owns him, He said: ﴿of His servants is All-Aware, All-Seeing﴾; i.e., He is knowing with the finest and most precise knowledge, of the inner states of them; ﴿All-Seeing﴾; i.e., of the outward aspects of their affairs and their inner aspects; that is, He settles fear and knowledge in the hearts according to what they were given of the Book, in its knowledge and its recitation, even if they appear to have the opposite of that. So you (O Messenger) are the most deserving of them of perfection, because you are the most fearful of them and the most God-conscious; therefore We gave you this Book, and the most fearful of them after you is the most deserving of its knowledge.

[p. 54] Since the meaning of the two descriptions is: We facilitate the recitation of Our Book for whoever is receptive to knowledge, which is the pillar of fear (of God), through what he learns from it by Our information and Our sight. And since the one who combined recitation with understanding reached the highest summit of knowledge, He said, coordinating (with what the context has guided us to estimate), pointing with the particle of distance to the high rank of the people of this category, who are this Ummah, the unlettered Ummah, despite the differences in their levels of inheritance and the lateness of their inheritance relative to those before them, and turning the speech toward the manifestation of greatness because the situation requires it, in removing something from one people and establishing it for others: ﴿Then We made inheritors﴾. That is, by Our greatness We granted them complete dominion and gave a gift that cannot be taken back. He expressed it regarding other than this Ummah with His saying: ﴿and they inherited the Book﴾ [al-A'raf: 169]. So observe the difference between the two expressions, and you will know the difference between the two situations. It is possible that the estimate is: "after We revealed to you and made you inherit it, then We made them inherit it," but He made it more evident in indicating the description, alerting to the completeness of its gathering of the previous books, and informing that "min" in "We revealed to you from" is explanatory. So He said: ﴿the Book﴾, that is, the Qur'an, by the consensus of the exegetes, as al-Asfahani said, which gathers every book We sent down, so it is the "mother" of every good. Ibn 'Abbas, as transmitted by Ibn al-Jawzi, said: Indeed God made the Ummah of Muhammad inherit every book He sent down. ﴿Those whom We have chosen﴾: that is, We acted in choosing them as one who strives in that matter. ﴿From among Our servants﴾: that is, We made them sincerely Ours. They are the Children of Isma'il and whoever follows them, meaning the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ), as al-Baghawi transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both). It is transmitted from Ibn Jarir that he said: "Inheritance" is the transfer of something from one people to another. So "then" here is for sequence, because the giving to this Ummah is delayed relative to the giving to the (earlier) nations, and its transfer to them occurred after the nullification of those religions and the abrogation of those books, except what agreed with the Qur'an. So the meaning of inheritance is that He removed those books from the earlier nations and gave them to this Ummah in the manner He was pleased with for it. And this inheritance is for the whole group; it does not require exclusivity to the one who memorizes the entire Qur'an, but includes whoever memorizes a part of it, even if only al-Fatihah. For the Companions, may Allah's good pleasure be upon them all, not each one of them memorized the entire Qur'an, and we are certain that they are among the chosen.

[p. 55] And since most people cannot be free of much shortcoming, because of the deficiency with which man has been created, whoever has this (deficiency) would remove himself from this category. So He said, informing him of his measure, comforting him with what He opened to him of His lights, drawing him to the presence of His holiness and the source of His secrets, dividing the people of this category, who are the people of understanding, into three divisions, beginning with the lowest because they are the most numerous, and so that despair does not arise and fear of the severity does not break hearts: ﴿So among them﴾: that is, because of Our inheritance to them, it resulted that there was among them, as is observed, ﴿one who wrongs himself﴾: that is, by negligence and laxity in fulfilling the right according to what his state requires of action, not guarding against major sins. This category is the majority of the inheritors, and they are those whose matter is deferred to Allah's command.

And since a person's abandonment of wrongdoing is extremely difficult, He drew attention to that with the form of the (reflexive) verb-pattern (ifti'al), so He said: ﴿And among them is one who is moderate﴾: that is, one who is intermediate in action, not expending all effort, except that he avoids major sins, so minor sins are expiated for him. They are those who mixed a righteous deed with another evil one. ﴿And among them is one foremost in good deeds﴾: that is, in acts of worship and all kinds of drawing near; one who fulfills the station in which he is placed its right; whenever he increases in nearness he increases in action, and he is not foremost unless he is like this. They are the foremost early ones among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them with excellence. This is supported by the saying of al-Hasan: "The foremost is the one whose good deeds outweigh (his bad)"; "the moderate is the one whose good and bad deeds are equal"; and "the wrongdoer is the one whose bad deeds outweigh (his good)." He ended with the foremost because they are the essence, and so that they would be closer to the gardens, just as He mentioned the monasteries first in Surat al-Hajj so that they would be closer to destruction, and delayed the mosques because of the closeness of the mention. In al-Tawbah He mentioned the foremost right after those of the nearness-seeking Bedouins, delayed the Murji'un, and followed them with the people of the mosque of harm. Glorified is He, in al-Ahzab, mentioned the Muslims first and elevated the address degree by degree up to "the men who remember Allah much" (al-Ahzab 35). So He, glorified be He, sometimes begins with the lowest and sometimes with the highest, according to what the situation requires, as is mentioned in this Book in its appropriate places. This (interpretation) is on the basis that the pronoun in "minhum" returns to "those whom We have chosen," not to the servants. It is supported by observation and by the context, since the people of knowledge are the reciters of the Book of Allah, and it is supported by hadiths that are not limited (in their chains), though they are weak with respect to their suitability to strengthen this. Among them is what al-Baghawi transmitted with his chain: "From Ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) that he recited this verse on the pulpit and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Our foremost is foremost, our moderate is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven.'" And with his chain, from Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him) that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse and said: 'As for the one foremost in good deeds, he will enter Paradise without reckoning; as for the moderate, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning; and as for the one who wrongs himself, he will be detained in the place of standing until grief reaches him, then he will enter Paradise.'" Then he recited: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us grief﴾ [Fatir: 34]. And it is transmitted without a chain, from Usama ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are all from this Ummah." Ibn al-Jawzi said, after mentioning the hadith of Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) without a chain: al-Tirmidhi transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding this verse, said: 'They are all in Paradise.'"

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir transmitted the hadith of Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him) in al-Kuna from Tarikh Dimashq, in the biography of the brother of Ziyad, or Abu Ziyad.

As for the pronoun returning to the servants, Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "The foremost is the sincere believer; the moderate is the showy one (who does deeds to be seen); and the wrongdoer is the disbeliever in Allah's blessing, not the one who denies it." Qatada said: "The wrongdoers are the companions of the left; the moderate are the companions of the right; and the foremost are those brought near."

And since this is not within the power of the servant in the ordinary course of things, and is not attained by acquisition and striving, He pointed to its greatness by His saying: ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾: that is, by the enabling of One who has complete power, general greatness, action by choice, and all attributes of perfection, and by His facilitating and making it easy, lest anyone feel secure from His plan (glorified be He). Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': "Then among the foremost is one who reaches the station of nearness and becomes absorbed in His oneness; he is the single one whose remembrance has made (the heavens and earth) tremble." End of quote. Then He increased the greatness of this matter in clarification, so He said, emphasizing, refuting the assumptions of the ignorant, because the foremost, whenever his station in precedence rises, his share of this world decreases, so the ignorant think he is squandering himself: ﴿That﴾: that is, the precedence, or the inheritance of the Book; ﴿it is﴾, pointing with the particle of distance, specifying with the pronoun of separation: ﴿the great bounty﴾.

When (Exalted is He) had mentioned their conditions, He explained their recompense and their final destination. So He said, beginning a new statement as an answer to one who asked about that: ﴿Gardens of 'Adn (perpetual residence)﴾. That is, they are caused by the cause of precedence, which is the bounty (al-fadl). It is also permissible for "Gardens" to be a substitute (badal) for "the bounty," because the bounty is its cause, so it is as though the bounty itself were the reward. ﴿'Adn﴾ means residence without departure, because there is no cause for departure from it. ﴿They will enter it﴾, that is, the three categories. Whoever enters it does not leave it, because nothing will remove him from it, and he himself does not wish to leave. This is on the reading that the pronoun refers to ﴿those﴾ (alladhina). Whoever takes the pronoun to refer to ﴿Our servants﴾ restricts the entering to the moderate (muqtasid) and the foremost (sabiq). This is on the reading of the canonical majority (Qira'at al-Jama'ah), with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the kha'. On the reading of Abu 'Amr, with the passive voice, the pronoun refers to the foremost alone, because they will be, at the time of reckoning, on dunes of musk and pulpits of light, and they will find their place pleasant. When they are called to Paradise they will delay, so they will be driven to it, as is mentioned at the end of Surat al-Zumar.

Since the one who enters a place first looks at the precious things in it, He said: ﴿They will be adorned therein﴾, that is, they will wear, as a form of adornment and ornamentation, ﴿with bracelets﴾. Since indefiniteness followed by specification gives the soul greater awe, and since the aim of the surah is to establish complete power in order to establish the most complete of the two perpetuities, He aroused desire for the obedience that leads to it by means of the finest ornaments we know. So He said, explaining the type of the bracelets: ﴿of gold and pearls﴾. Since such finery is only fitting with splendid clothing, He said, informing that they will be clothed when they enter: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾.

(p-٦٠) Since the moderate (*al-muqtasid*) and the foremost (*al-sabiq*) grieve, because of their perfection and their intense compassion for the wrongdoer when he is requited, he gathered them together and said, expressing it in the past tense to affirm it: ﴿And they will say﴾, i.e., upon their entering: ﴿Praise be to God﴾, i.e., the encompassing of the attributes of perfection; ﴿to God﴾, i.e., the One who possesses complete power; ﴿who has removed from us﴾, i.e., by our entering this place; ﴿the grief﴾, i.e., this kind of grief in its entirety. So we shall not grieve over anything that had escaped us, and there will never be any grief for us, because we have come to an abode in which nothing is lost at all, nor does it perish.

Since they knew the transgressions, slips, or heedlessnesses they had committed, which, were it not for generosity, would have led them to the Fire, they gave the reason for what they had attained through them by saying, with emphasis, to make known the joy they had over the pardon of their sins, and that what they emphasized deserves to be stressed greatly, because they saw its soundness and tasted the sweetness of its fruit: ﴿Indeed our Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to us despite our wrongdoing; ﴿is All-Forgiving﴾, i.e., One who erases sins, both their essence and their traces, for the first two categories; ﴿All-Appreciative﴾, i.e., in return for what He bestowed upon the servant of good obedience, and granted him success in good deeds, so that He made him, by this, among the foremost.

Then they described Him with what is itself an expression of gratitude, saying: ﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence (al-muqama)﴾; that is, of residence (al-iqama), both its place and its time, in which the one who dwells does not desire to depart from it, despite the great number of those who dwell there, and no departure is intended for him; and nothing in it passes away so that one would grieve over it.

Since the absolute Owner is under no obligation, and His servant has no claim upon Him in any respect, He said: ﴿out of His bounty﴾; that is, without any work on our part. For our good deeds were only a favor from Him, may He be glorified; had He not stirred us to them and made them easy for us, they would not have existed.

When they recalled what they had witnessed in the plains of the Resurrection of those hardships, terrors, griefs and burdens, to which His saying (exalted is He) alludes: ﴿And if one heavily laden calls out for its load﴾ [Fatir: 18], and so on, they resumed their statement describing the abode of settlement: ﴿No fatigue touches us in it﴾; that is, at any moment whatsoever; ﴿nor does weariness touch us in it﴾; that is, exhaustion, toil, fatigue, and lassitude of soul from any of the things. Abu Hayyan said: "It is a consequence of bodily toil." So it is, by my life, the one most worthy of having it said of it:

Yellow (safra') — sorrows never alight upon its courtyard; ** were a stone to touch it, it would be touched by joy.

When he had explained what they enjoy of blessing, he explained what their enemies have of retribution, to add to their joy at what they endured in this world of their arrogance toward them and their wickedness. So He said: ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: those who concealed what their intellects pointed to of the suns of the signs and the lights of the proofs. ﴿For them is the Fire of Hell﴾, meaning: because they scowled at (tajahhamū) the friends of God, the callers to Him. Since the usual way of the Fire is to destroy whoever enters it quickly, he explained that its state is other than this, to add to their punishment and their evil end. So He said, as a resumption (mustani'fan): ﴿It will not be decreed for them﴾, meaning: it will not be ruled, executed, or established by any judge upon them, ﴿so that they die﴾ (fa-yamūtū), meaning: so that their death results from the decree. If you consult what preceded in the Surah "Subḥān" (al-Isrā'), from His saying: ﴿they have no power to remove the harm from you﴾ [al-Isrā' 17:56], and what will come, God willing (Exalted is He), in "al-Mursalāt", from His saying: ﴿nor are they permitted, so that they make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalāt 77:36], you will know the secret of the obligation of the accusative (naṣb) here (i'rāb: the grammatical case), because if it were in the nominative, the meaning would be that their death is required whether or not a decree is issued against them, and that is impossible.

Since the hardships of this world are relieved, however long their term, He said: ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾, and He went further in negation with His saying: ﴿from its punishment﴾, meaning: of Hell. Since it might be supposed that this punishment is specific to the disbelievers of his time (ﷺ), He said: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning: like this great recompense, ﴿We recompense﴾, meaning: by what We possess of greatness, according to the reading of the majority, with the nūn (we), ﴿every ungrateful one﴾, meaning: ungrateful toward him (ﷺ), or toward other prophets, peace be upon them, even if he did not see him, because the establishment of the miracle is equal for hearing and sight. Abū 'Amr constructed the verb in the passive, as an indication of its ease and facility, and he put "every" (kull) in the nominative.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 35, verse 37:

When he had explained their punishment, he explained their lamentation, saying: ﴿And they﴾; that is, He did this to them while the state was that they ﴿cry out for help therein﴾; that is, they bring forth the shouting therein with the utmost effort they are capable of in crying out, with weeping and wailing. When he had explained that, he explained their words in their outcry by saying: ﴿Our Lord﴾; that is, they say: O Benefactor to us; ﴿bring us out﴾; that is, from the Fire; ﴿we will do righteousness﴾. Then they emphasized it, explained it and made it clear by their saying, as an expression of regret and an admission of error (or because they used to think their deeds were righteous): ﴿other than what we used to do﴾; that is, with the utmost of our effort; ﴿we did﴾. So they neglected softening their hearts and acting according to its measure at the time when it would benefit, and they employed it only when its time had passed, so it did not benefit them. Rather, it was said in reply to them, as a confirmation to them, a rebuke and a reproach: ﴿Did We not﴾; that is, were you not in the abode of action, empowered to do that by your intellects and faculties? Did We not ﴿give you life﴾; that is, lengthen your lifespans, while We gave you intellects and did not hasten to seize you; ﴿for what﴾; that is, a time; ﴿in which one who would take heed could take heed﴾; and this includes every lifespan in which the accountable person is able to set right his affairs. Yet the rebuke is greater for a long life. And by the mention of the attribute of Majesty He indicated that there is no hope, apart from Him - glory be to Him - of extending the lifespan.

Since reflection after the Resurrection is not beneficial, because it is after the removal of the veil, He expressed it in the past tense, saying: ﴿whoever took heed﴾; to inform that He has already sealed the register of those who take heed, so no one will be added to them. The period referred to is said to be sixty years; this was said by Ibn 'Abbas - may Allah be pleased with them both. Al-Bukhari gave it a chapter heading at the beginning of ar-Riqaq without attributing it to anyone. Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated from Abu Hurayrah - may Allah be pleased with him - that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever Allah has allowed to live sixty years, Allah has left him no excuse regarding his lifespan." At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Abu Ya'la also narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The lifespans of my ummah are between sixty and seventy, and few of them pass beyond that."

When he had pointed to the rational proof, both at the start and continuing, he pointed to the textual proofs that alert to what reason falls short of; so he said, expressing it in the past tense to make the intended meaning explicit, in conjunction with the sense of "Did We not give you life?", which is "We have indeed given you life": ﴿And there came to you the warner﴾; that is, from Me, through the messengers and the books, as a support for reason with the rational evidence.

When it followed from this that their punishment would never cease, He said: ﴿So taste﴾; that is, what We have prepared for you of punishment, forever and ever. And since it is the custom that whoever despairs of his adversary turns to seeking help against him, this followed by His saying: ﴿so there is not﴾; the original would have been "for you", but He made it apparent, attaching the judgment to the attribute for generality, so He said: ﴿for the wrongdoers﴾; that is, those who place things other than in their proper places; ﴿any helper﴾; that is, one who would aid them and strengthen their hands. So there is no escape for you from this tasting. This is general for every wrongdoer, for whoever persists in wrongdoing will be overcome, since his wrongdoing weakens and diminishes every day, while the truth grows stronger and greater at every moment.

(p-65) Since He, glorified is He, knows what He negated and what He affirmed, He gave the reason for that, establishing the cause of the continuation of their punishment, and that it is in proportion to their disbelief, as He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And the recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40]. He did so with His saying, emphasizing it, as an indication that it is not obligatory to train the soul upon it, because of its difficulty, since the soul is bound to sensible things. ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, ﴿is Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾. Since the direction of height is more deeply rooted in the unseen, He said "of the heavens and the earth." From this he derived His saying, emphasizing it, because it is among the most wondrous of the unseen, for what is in a person's self is often hidden from him, while Allah (exalted is He) knows it. Or it is a reason for what precedes it: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, that is, with a knowledge that is complete; ﴿within the breasts﴾, that is, before its owners know it, when it is pure unseen. He knows that if your lives were prolonged you would never turn back from disbelief, and that if you were returned you would return to what you were forbidden; and that there is no hope for your reform. For this reason He commands the angel, when the spirit is breathed into the fetus, to write that he is either wretched or blessed, before he has any thought at all. Sometimes he is at the utmost of inclining toward good, in deed and intention, and then his end is concluded with evil; and sometimes it is the opposite, in the utmost of corruption, leaving no polytheism or other sins until he commits them; yet with Allah he is blessed, because of what He knows of his intention afterward, when he turns his heart to Him, so his end is concluded with good (p-66), and he becomes one of the people of Paradise. As for thoughts after they have come into existence in the hearts, the angel and the devil may perceive them.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 35, verse 39:**

Since whoever originates a thing has the fullest knowledge of it, and the perfection of its making indicates the completeness of its Maker's power, and the completeness of His power necessarily entails the completeness of His knowledge, He said: ﴿He﴾, that is, He alone, not your partners nor anyone else, ﴿who made you﴾, that is, O people, ﴿successors (khala'if)﴾. This is the plural of *khalifa* (successor, one who takes the place of another), which is one who stands after a person in what that person was standing in. The plural *khulafa'* is the plural of *khalif*. So said al-Asfahani. Al-Qushayri said: The people of every age are successors to those who preceded them. Some people are a beauty to their predecessors, and some people are the lowest and most worthless. The virtuous of their time are a trial for them, and the worthless are a trial for their time.

Since the intention is to diminish the matter of their partners, and this is achieved by removing their power over what He, glorified is He, granted the worshippers on the earth, He brought in the prepositional phrase to show that they, despite their large numbers and the extension of their eras, do not fill their dwelling with their management, because He causes each generation to die and substitutes those who come after them in their place. Had He not caused them to die, the earth would not have contained them with continued reproduction over a long time, while they were originally a small piece of its dust. So He said: ﴿on the earth﴾, that is, in that part of it in which you are, not elsewhere, ﴿you dispose of it by what you have power over﴾. Had He willed, He would not have let you dispose of it. So it is your duty to thank Him and not to disbelieve in Him.

[p. 67]

Since it is established that this is a blessing from Him, in that He granted them a lifespan in which whoever will be mindful may remember, the following is said as a consequence: ﴿Whoever disbelieves﴾, that is, after knowing that God is the One who empowered him, not anyone else, and belittles this exalted blessing, ﴿then upon him is his disbelief﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿his disbelief﴾, that is, his harm. Since the state of a thing being upon another thing may admit of several matters, he clarified its condition by His saying, emphasizing it for the sake of one who may imagine that the expansion of worldly provision upon the wicked person is profit and an honor from God to him: ﴿And not﴾, that is, while the state is that it does not ﴿increase the disbelievers﴾, that is, those who cover the truth, ﴿their disbelief﴾, that is, the one they are engaged in, thinking that it makes them happy, while they are firmly rooted in it and are not able to be detached from it. For this reason He did not say "does not increase whoever disbelieves," because his disbelief may not be firmly rooted, so he may become a Muslim. ﴿With their Lord﴾, that is, the One who benefits them, ﴿except in hatred﴾, that is, because He treats them as one who hates and despises them, with the utmost hatred and contempt.

Since the intention of these attributes with regard to God, exalted is He, is their ends, and their mention is only a depiction of them in their most terrible forms, to increase aversion to their causes, and since they used to marry their fathers' wives while calling it "the marriage of hatred," He drew attention to the fact that they do not care about being hated by the Benefactor. So He said, mentioning the end and clarifying that the target of their gaze [p. 68] is financial loss, debasing their resolves and increasing their rebuke: ﴿And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss﴾, that is, the ones most deeply entrenched in the attribute of covering the truth, ﴿except in loss﴾, that is, in this world and the Hereafter, in wealth and in self. This is the extreme of what the one who hates does to the one who is hated.

Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, commentary on Surah 35, verse 40:

When He - glorified is He - had made clear that it is He who made them successors, He confirmed this explanation to them by commanding His Messenger (ﷺ) with what would compel them to acknowledge it. So He said: ﴿Say: Tell me about your partners﴾, that is, inform me. ﴿Your partners﴾: He attributed them to them because, although they had made them His partners, they gained no share of His partnership, since they had not diminished anything of His dominion. They had only shared with the worshippers in their wealth, through its impurities and otherwise, and in their deeds. So they are truly their partners, not His partners. Then He explained what is meant by their counting them as partners in His words: ﴿Whom you call upon﴾, that is, whom you call upon as partners, ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection.

Since the implied meaning is: "By what did you make them partners in worship? Do they have a share in the earth?" He built upon it His words, repeating them to make them witness the incapacity of their partners and the deficiency of those they worshipped besides Him: ﴿Show me what﴾, that is, which, or what thing, ﴿they have created of the earth﴾, that is, so that your claim of partnership with them may be valid. Otherwise your claim concerning them is pure falsehood, while you claim that you are the furthest of people from it in trivial matters, so how about such a matter?! Perhaps their asking about seeing their partners is an alert that they are of such abasement and worthlessness that everyone who intends to see them sees them, and knows that they have no creative power, whereas Allah (Exalted is He) is the opposite in both respects: He is clothed in the mantle of greatness and veiled by the veil of majesty and might, and everyone knows that He is the Creator of every created thing. So how can One who creates not be like One who creates?!

When He alerted them with this matter, which the teacher (al-Mu'allim) brought forward, namely that it is not fitting for any intelligent person to claim a partnership in something unless he knows the partnership, even if he is ignorant of the specific party sharing in it, He said, confirming this, widening for them the fields of argument, increasing their rebuke for the error they are in: ﴿Or do they have a share﴾, that is, even if it is small, ﴿in the heavens?﴾, that is, show me what they created in the heavens. So the verse is an instance of *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which something is omitted from one part of a statement because its counterpart is mentioned in another part): He first omitted the question about partnership in the earth, because a similar mention in the heavens indicates it, and He omitted the command to show, the second time, because a similar mention the first time indicates it.

When He completed the rebuke by questioning about what is seen, He followed it with reproach by questioning about what is heard, signalling a shift (*iltifat*, a change of grammatical person) to the first person of speech, in the manner of majesty, with severe anger. So He said: ﴿Or have We given them﴾, that is, the partners, or those who associate others with Him, ﴿a Book﴾, that is, indicating that it is from Us by its inimitability or by other decisive proofs, ﴿so that they stand upon a clear proof from it﴾, that is, a manifest evidence; and "clear proofs" (*bayyinat*) in another reading (*qira'ah*), that is, clear indications, through the various kinds of clarification contained in that Book, ﴿from it﴾, that is, from that Book, by which We have made them partners in the matter, so that they might testify for them this testimony, which they would not accept as proof of partnership for any of their own slaves in the most trivial things. So how would they accept it in diminishing the King, from whom they have no good except through Him, not fearing Him and not ashamed before Him?

Since the implied meaning is: "None of that exists, so they have no clear proof, but rather [they have] delusion," He said, alerting them to the blameworthiness of their states, the foolishness of their opinions, the baseness of their aspirations, and the deficiency of their intellects, informing that they are unable to bring anything of what they are demanded, and that they have no answer to what they are asked about. He emphasized it because of their assumption that their affairs are in the utmost firmness: ﴿Nay, the wrongdoers promise one another﴾, that is, those who place things in other than their proper places, ﴿nothing but delusion﴾, that is, the followers to the leaders, that their partners will bring them near to Allah in nearness, and that they will intercede and harm and not benefit.

When He had shown the insignificance of the idols and everything they associated with Him, relative to the majesty of His greatness, and since they were unable to claim any partnership in creation in any respect, and since one of them, or someone else, might perhaps be stubborn enough to make such a claim, and since people had come to know some of the celestial changes, such as sunrise, sunset, and eclipses, but had no knowledge of earthquakes or the decline of the sun from its zenith (al-zawal), He said, showing His greatness, glorified is He, after belittling the matter of their partners, as a challenge to them and a warning against their undertaking this great fabrication, showing the blessing of not being hastened with destruction, and emphasizing it because among people there are those who deny it, namely the *mu'attilah* (those who deny God's attributes), and among them are those whose conduct, even if they affirm it, is the conduct of deniers, namely those who deny some aspect of His power, such as resurrection:

﴿Indeed, God holds back the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾; that is, the One who possesses all attributes of perfection; ﴿holds back the heavens﴾; that is, despite their vastness and height; ﴿and the earth﴾; that is, despite its extent and its distance from being held together; as you witness, a holding back that prevents ﴿them from ceasing﴾; that is, from a great tremor and a severe quake, or from a cessation in which no stability remains. For their staying in the state they are in is beyond all measure, were it not for the towering power of His might and the dazzling force of His honour and greatness. So if you claim, out of obstinacy, that your partners cannot create for any reason, then call upon them to remove what God has created, glorified is He.

Since this is evidence that both of them are created and perishable, He followed it with something clearer than it, saying, expressing it with the particle of possibility:

﴿And if they should cease﴾; that is, through a quake or ruin; ﴿were anyone to hold them back﴾; that is, anyone other than Him. He emphasized the comprehensiveness of the negation with His words ﴿anyone﴾. Since the meaning is that other than Him, glorified is He, is unable to hold them back for any period of time, however brief, He affirmed the preposition, saying ﴿after Him﴾; that is, after He has removed them. Indeed, when the earth is shaken, everything upon it is disturbed, and the idols are among its contents. This clearly indicates that the partners are acted upon, not acting agents.

Since the context leans more toward encouraging turning to Him alone than toward warning, and it was as if it were said: He is worthy of removing them for the great sins their people commit and the severe crimes they perpetrate, He said, as an answer to that and emphasizing it, because judging what the falsifiers perpetrate, despite its magnitude and their multitude, is something the intellects cannot contain:

﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing﴾; that is, eternally and everlastingly; ﴿Forbearing﴾; that is, it is not part of His nature to hasten punishment for the disobedient, for one hastens only when one fears missing the opportunity, and so seizes the chances. He also encouraged repentance, indicating that He does not possess what forbearing humans have of narrowness, which leads them, when they become angry after long patience, to not forgive, by His saying:

﴿Oft-Forgiving﴾; that is, the One who effaces the sins of whoever returns to Him and turns to Him in acknowledgment, so He neither punishes him nor reproaches him.

(p-73) When the presumed sense was: "They said: We do not claim that they created anything of the heavens or of the earth, and we acknowledge that none holds the heavens and the earth except God; we only worship them so that they bring us near to God in nearness, as our fathers used to do, and had they not had a proof for that, they would not have done it," He followed it with His words, which clarify their error in denying the messengers after the error they had already shown in associating partners with the One who sent them, while He grants them respite and provides for them, as a sign of His forbearance together with His knowledge: ﴿And they swore by God﴾, that is, the Meccan unbelievers, ﴿by God﴾, that is, the One besides whom there is no truly great one, ﴿with their most solemn oaths﴾, that is, with the utmost of the oaths they were capable of. Al-Baghawi said: When it reached them, meaning the Meccan unbelievers, that the People of the Book had denied their messengers, they said: "May God curse the Jews and the Christians! Their messengers came to them and they denied them. If a messenger came to us, we would surely be better guided in religion than they are."

When He reported their oath, He stated the sense of what they swore to, without its wording, saying: ﴿If a warner came to them﴾, and He expressed it by the greatest cause of prophethood, so He said: ﴿warner﴾, that is, from God; ﴿they would surely be﴾, that is, the unbelievers would be; ﴿better guided﴾, that is, greater in guidance; ﴿than any one of the nations﴾, that is, of the past nations; or [it means] than the nation which had not received warners, that it would be better guided than those nations that had received warners. Abu Hayyan said: Just as they say: "He is one of the two best [ahad al-ahadayn]," and "She is one of the best [ihda al-uhad]," meaning superiority in cunning and intellect, because they had keener minds, more eloquent tongues, greater intellects, were more committed to what reason calls for, and more eager for what witnesses to excellence. They reinforced it with an oath, because the one who observes the denial of the People of Knowledge of the Book would deny them in their claim of confirmation, by way of an ukhrawi qiyas (a syllogistic inference, in which the conclusion follows from premises). He indicated their haste in lying with the fa' (the particle "then"), so He said: ﴿But when a warner came to them﴾, that is, as they had stipulated, and more; he was Muhammad (ﷺ), whom they used to witness to be the best of them in person, the most noble of them in lineage, the most generous of them in every character, both maternally and paternally, and the strongest of them in every distinction by his connections. ﴿It only increased them﴾, that is, his coming added nothing to their condition except ﴿aversion﴾, that is, because he became a cause of their increase in disbelief, like camels that had fled from their herdsman, strayed from the path, then he called them, and their aversion increased because of his call, so they went deeper into error, until it became difficult, or hard, to bring them back. Thus it becomes clear that they have no covenant, despite their claim that they are the most faithful of people, and that there is no truthfulness among them, despite their certainty that they are the most truthful of creatures.

(p-75) Since they had been created inclined toward misguidance, and aversion may arise from a praiseworthy or permissible matter, He gave the reason for it in His words: ﴿out of arrogance﴾, that is, seeking to produce greatness for themselves ﴿in the land﴾, that is, the land whose nature is lowliness (p-75) and humility and obscurity. ﴿And the evil scheming﴾, that is, because of their scheming, the scheme which by its nature harms its doer and others. It was their intention to extinguish the affair of the Prophet ﷺ and to put out the light of God. The reading of ʿAbd Allah, "wa-makran sayyi'an" (a scheme that is evil), indicates that it is an annexation of a thing to its attribute. The reading of Hamzah with the hamzah pronounced as sukun, with the intention of pausing (waqf, pausing at the end of a word), indicates their precision in scheming, their perfecting of it, and their concealing of their effort. ﴿And it does not encompass﴾, that is, while the case is that it does not ﴿encompass﴾, that is, surround with a binding and harmful encompassing, ﴿the evil scheming﴾, that is, the scheme which is deeply rooted in evil, ﴿except its people﴾. Even if it harms others besides its people, it does not encompass those others. From al-Zuhri that he said: "It has reached us that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Do not scheme, and do not help a schemer, for God says this verse. And do not transgress, and do not help a transgressor; God says: ﴿Your transgression is only against yourselves﴾ [Yunus 10:23]. And do not break oaths, and do not help one who breaks oaths; God says: ﴿Whoever breaks his oath, breaks it only against himself﴾ [al-Fath 48:10].'"

Since this was the custom of God which admits no change, He said, giving it as a consequence of that: ﴿Then do they await?﴾, that is, do they wait for it? Perhaps He used the verb without an object to indicate the swiftness of retribution against the scheming arrogant. It is possible that it is from looking with the eye, because it resembles knowledge of retribution against the earlier peoples, along with the knowledge that his habit is continuous, since nothing prevents him from it, due to the greatness of its certainty, the intensity of its firmness, and the strength of its presence through a sensible, present thing, of which nothing else is looked at in past or future, because everything else in relation to it is non-existence. Since their receiving of that was made a waiting on their part for it, and the interrogative was (p-76) denunciatory, it had the meaning of negation. He said: ﴿except the custom of the former peoples﴾, that is, their way in the swiftness of God's seizing them and sending down punishment upon them.

Since this looking requires clarity of intellect and sharpness of soul, He turned from their pronoun to addressing the highest of creation, as an alert that this is a station which no one other than him tastes in its true taste. Then, on the basis of the restriction of looking or waiting to this, He said, emphasizing it, because the disbelievers firmly believe that they will not change from their state and that the believers will not prevail over them: ﴿So you will not find﴾, that is, at all, at any time, ﴿for the custom of God﴾, that is, the way of the Greatest King which He legislated and by which He judged, which is the destruction of the disobedient and the deliverance of the obedient, ﴿any alteration﴾, that is, from anyone who would bring another custom other than it to be a substitute for it, because there is no equal to Him. ﴿And you will not find for the custom of God﴾, that is, which no one has any command against, ﴿any transformation﴾, that is, from one state into another that is more hidden than it, because there is no reversal of His decree, since He has no peer.

In the verse there is also that most of the talk of the soul is falsehood. So it is not fitting for anyone to think well of himself, nor to decide about the unseen except by attaching it to the will (of God), disavowing power and strength, perhaps God will grant him safety in its outcome.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 35, verse 44:

When he had made clear that their state necessitates (the punishment), and that it is inevitable that they be struck down, due to what has been established of the Days of Allah (ayyam Allah), and he had rebuked them for this, the implied sense was: "Have they not heard the reports of the earlier peoples, the oft-repeated (accounts), and their continuing states, with no exception at all in that whoever denied a messenger was seized?" Thus He said, linking it to what precedes and offering it as evidence for the report about His practice (sunnah) regarding the earlier peoples, through what is mentioned of their traces: ﴿Have they not traveled﴾, i.e., in past time; ﴿in the land﴾, i.e., the lands to which they journeyed for trade, in Syria, Yemen and Iraq; ﴿so that they might look﴾, i.e., so that as a result of that travel there might recur to them a look and a lesson on some day, for the intelligent person is one who, when he sees something, reflects upon it until he understands what the tongue of its state speaks, even if what its speech has conveyed is hidden from him. By placing it in the interrogative form he indicated that because of its greatness it went beyond its like, and so it deserved the question about its state: ﴿how was the end of﴾, i.e., the final outcome of ﴿those﴾ ... And since the ends of destruction were in some of the past times, he affirmed the preposition, saying: ﴿before them﴾, i.e., in whatever state their seizure was, so that they would know that they were seized only for denying the messengers, and so fear lest they do the like of their deeds, and their state become like theirs. This is the meaning of (Surah) Ya-Sin: ﴿that they to them do not return﴾ [Ya-Sin: 31], the same, as its explanation will come, God willing (exalted is He). And since the context concerned their being characterized by two strengths, that of outward (power), from arrogance, and that of inward (power), from harmful deceit, He established the strength of those whom He had warned with the like of their fate, by describing them with superiority, in a circumstantial clause, saying: ﴿and they were﴾, i.e., We destroyed them for their denial of Our messengers, while the state was that they were ﴿mightier than them﴾, i.e., than these (people); ﴿in strength﴾, in the two strengths of arrogance and deceit, which drag them after shame into the Fire.

And since the implied sense was: "Never has the affair of a nation of them outdone Allah, nor the affair of anyone of a nation when they denied their messenger; and no friend of his has failed, nor has any enemy of his profited," He joined to it His saying, emphasizing, as a sign of (the disbelievers') denial in their certainty that their religion does not change and that they will never be overcome, because of the abundance and capacity they have, and the paucity and weakness of the Muslims: ﴿And Allah is not such that He would ever be incapable﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs all greatness; he emphasized the comprehensiveness of the negation by His saying: ﴿to render Him incapable﴾, i.e., intending to render Him incapable. And since the will for incapacity was negated in Him, incapacity was negated by way of priority; and he intensified the emphasis by His saying: ﴿of anything﴾, i.e., small or great, and generalized with what reaches our perception by His saying: ﴿in the heavens﴾, i.e., the direction of height; and he emphasized by repeating the negation, saying: ﴿nor in the earth﴾, i.e., the direction of depth. And since the source of incapacity is ignorance, he gave the reason by His saying, emphasizing what was mentioned at the beginning of the verse: ﴿Indeed He is ever﴾, i.e., from eternity to eternity, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, i.e., of all-encompassing knowledge, ﴿All-Powerful﴾, i.e., of complete power; so He does not will a thing except that it is.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 35, verse 45:

When they used to ask for hastening of the threatened punishment, mockingly, saying: "What is wrong with Him that He does not destroy us?", it was known that the implied meaning is: "If Allah dealt with you according to the manner of one who takes to account, He would hasten your destruction." Then He followed it with His statement, to make the ruling manifest together with the knowledge of it: ﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to account﴾; that is, by what belongs to Him of the attributes of exaltedness; ﴿mankind﴾; that is, whoever has a stirring (nawas), meaning movement and agitation, among those who are responsible (mukallaf), in general.

Since the context here concerns the actions of the limbs (af'al al-jawarih), because the scheming (makr) and arrogance (kibr) are disliked only for their effects and not for the attribute of being characterized by them, unlike the context of Surah al-Nahl, for it prohibits the attribute itself even if no effect of the limbs appears from it, here He expressed it with "kasb" (earning/acquiring), and He detached the verbal noun (masdar) to restrict what has come into existence from them to the act; so He said: ﴿for what they earned﴾; that is, from all their deeds, whether it was unlawful or not; ﴿He would not leave upon its back﴾; that is, the earth; ﴿any creature﴾; that is, rather He would destroy them all. As for the responsible ones, it is because there is nothing in their deeds which He, glory be to Him, would measure at its true measure, due to the deficiency that is in them, and due to what He, glory be to Him, has of exaltedness, elevation, and perfection. As for others, they were created for them, and sins remove blessings and bring down retributions. This is what He did in the time of Noah, peace be upon him: none was saved from those who were on the earth except those who were in the Ark. ﴿But﴾; He did not deal with them according to the manner of one who takes to account and scrutinizes; rather He is forbearing toward them, so He ﴿defers them﴾; that is, in the worldly life, then in the barzakh; ﴿until a specified term﴾; that is, which He named in eternity, for the expiry of their lifespans, then for their resurrection from their graves. He does not alter the word with Him, due to the attributes He has, which are, to you, the most wondrous of the wondrous, because you do not perceive them with true perception. ﴿So when their term comes﴾; that is, the term of annihilation and extinction, He takes each one of them at his term; or the term of existence and preservation, He resurrects each of them, and recompenses him for his deed without error or incapacity.

Since they denied what this entails of resurrection, He emphasized, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾; that is, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, the Originator with complete power and perfect choice; ﴿has always been﴾; and never ceased; and since the context concerns earning, which is more general than wrongdoing, He said: ﴿with His servants﴾; whom He brought into existence, and none has a partner with Him in the bringing into existence of any of them, in their entire selves and conditions; ﴿Seeing﴾; that is, of penetrating sight and knowledge, of who deserves punishment from them by their earning, and who deserves reward. Thus its ending has, as you see, corresponded to its beginning, by comprehending the attributes of perfection and complete power over each of bringing into existence and annihilation, for animate and inanimate beings, whatever He wills, by choice, as is witnessed of His effects, glory be to Him; as the guidance to this occurred through the command to travel and by other means, and through what the surah was concluded with, the attribute of knowledge, in a manner more eloquent than mentioning it by its name, as was passed in Surah Ta-Ha, that the comprehensiveness of knowledge entails the all-encompassing nature of power, and power is not all-encompassing except when it is by choice. Thus His entitlement to all praises is established at that point, (Exalted is He). From Him, glory be to Him, came the mighty messages, comprising might and wisdom, through the angels who are stripped of desires and every share, to whoever among mankind is suited to them, by the overcoming of the army of his intellect over the hosts of his desires and soul, until it becomes a pure, stripped intellect, governing over desires and shares, dominant, sufficient.
